jnanalytics

Open data about the journal market in transformative agreements: which journals are covered, whether they are hybrid or fully open access, how much they publish, how much of it is openly licensed, how complete the metadata is, and how many articles fall under an agreement.

jnanalytics succeeds hoaddata. It builds one tidy data model in Google BigQuery from two open sources only, Crossref and OpenAlex, using the journal and institution lists of the cOAlition S Journal Checker Tool and the ESAC registry. The dashboard, a browser-based data explorer and BigQuery users all read the same tables.

Installation

From a clone of the repository:

devtools::install()

Three ways to the data

Layer Tables How
Package data Reference tables: journals, journal_issns, agreements, agreement_journals, agreement_institutions, portfolios library(jnanalytics)
Parquet export Reference tables and journal-level aggregates (about 50 MB), in parquet/ of this repository, one version per release jn_source("parquet") in a clone, or download single files
BigQuery subugoe-collaborative.jn_analytics All tables, including the article level jn_source("bigquery")

Examples

The analysis functions run unchanged on the Parquet files and on BigQuery. By default they count research articles (OpenAlex types article and review) in all journals.

library(jnanalytics)
src <- jn_source("parquet")

# Open access in hybrid and fully OA journals over time
jn_oa(src, by = c("pub_year", "oa_model"))

# Licences in the hybrid journals of the Wiley portfolio, German first authors
jn_licenses(src, portfolio = "wiley", country = "DE", oa_model = "hybrid")

# Crossref metadata coverage by OA model
jn_metadata(src, by = c("pub_year", "oa_model"))

# Article-level data is only in BigQuery
bq <- jn_source("bigquery")
jn_tbl(bq, "articles") |>
  dplyr::filter(issn_l == "0360-0300", pub_year == 2025) |>
  dplyr::collect()

Data model

Every table, column and counting rule is documented in one schema (inst/schema/columns.csv), available as jn_schema() and described in vignette("data-model"). The same descriptions are set on the BigQuery columns and stored in the Parquet metadata.

Building the data

The build is a targets pipeline (_targets.R) that only reruns steps whose inputs changed:

  1. Copy the current JCT files (jct_jn_all.csv, jct_inst_all.csv, esac_df.csv) from the jct_data scraper into data-raw/, and gzip the journal list (gzip -9 data-raw/jct_jn_all.csv).
  2. Run targets::tar_make() locally, or start the build workflow in GitHub Actions.

The pipeline rebuilds the reference tables, the BigQuery tables and the Parquet export as needed. The workflow commits the updated reference data and Parquet files, so every release is versioned in this repository. A full rebuild scans about 245 GB in BigQuery.

Development note

This package was developed with the help of Claude Code, Anthropic’s AI coding assistant. Design decisions, counting rules and results were specified and reviewed by the maintainer; the data were checked against the previous hoaddata release.
